criteria.reason: Fuses statistics and moral claims into one advocacy verdict; labels its basis but does not separate empirical questions from the moral judgement.
Claims 'no credible evidence' of deterrence, effectively disproven; the 2012 NRC review actually found the evidence inconclusive.
One-sided abolitionist case; disclaims personal opinion yet delivers a flat verdict without opposing arguments or contested-question framing.
Figures check out: 190+ US death-row exonerations since 1973; roughly 70% of countries abolitionist in law or practice.

factual_errors: Mischaracterizes the 2012 NRC deterrence review as showing no deterrent effect; the review found the research inconclusive
summary: Takes a firm abolitionist stand (Reading A) but presents it as a fact forced by evidence, claims deterrence is disproven rather than inconclusive, gives one-sided arguments, and mischaracterizes the NRC review; cited statistics are accurate.
